posts.title: Distributed primary keys
posts.description: On a single Postgres server, primary keys stay unique because only one sequence hands out the numbers: a bigint identity column asks it for the next one, and no two rows ever get the same. Now put writers in several regions, each of them accepting inserts while the links between them are slow or down. posts.title: Postgres logical replication beyond one writer
posts.description: In 2014, if you wanted Postgres servers on several continents, each of them accepting writes and all of them sharing their rows, there was one serious open source answer: BDR, from 2ndQuadrant. It needed a patched PostgreSQL 9.4 and a plugin, which means it needed a server that was not Postgres.
